label: copy-phase input u (fed-back u from original position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, and only when the input token is u, i.e. the model is feeding back an original u. It is almost entirely restricted to u at original position >= 2 (recall_idx >= 3). A fed-back u from original position 1 (recall_idx 2) fires only weakly (0.7% of mass), and u at position 0 never fires. It never fires on u in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token. Weak or absent firings (false positives) mostly come from a u near the end of short sequences. In the top examples the strongest activations come where the original has a run of u (u u): the first fed-back u of the run is near max, and the next one is lower. Magnitude is not controlled by the identity of the output token.

issues: The test score reproduces: P 0.948, R 0.974, F1 0.961, mass recall 0.993. The profile confirms the main claims: 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase and 100% is on in_tok u. Recall_idx 0 and 1 never fire. Recall_idx 2 (a fed-back u from original position 1) holds 0.7% of the mass. Activation magnitude is flat across out_tok values.
The missed activations (1448 on test) are mostly weak firings on a fed-back u from position 1 (recall_idx 2). This matches the explanation, and they are low-mass noise.

One small inaccuracy: the false positives are not really 'near the end of short sequences'. Precision is lowest when to_go == 0, i.e. on the last step (0.91 vs about 0.96 elsewhere), and also at L == 4 (0.85). In absolute terms, though, last-step false positives with L >= 6 (about 1000) outnumber those with L <= 5 (about 440). Precision never drops low enough to call this a systematic class, so it does not justify a new predicate.
The run-of-u claim fits: when the previous input is also u, precision is 0.987, and in the top examples the second u of a run fires but lower. No overclaim was found.
